hook.en: Turning a radio's tuning knob changes a capacitor until the circuit resonates with one station's frequency, and the current from that station shoots up. That is series LCR resonance.
hook.kn: ರೇಡಿಯೊದ ಟ್ಯೂನಿಂಗ್ ಗುಂಡಿ ತಿರುಗಿಸಿದಾಗ ಧಾರಕ ಬದಲಾಗಿ ಮಂಡಲವು ಒಂದು ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಅನುನಾದಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಆ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಗರಿಷ್ಠವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದೇ ಶ್ರೇಣಿ LCR ಅನುನಾದ.

objectives.en: Find the impedance and phase angle of a series LCR circuit.
Find the resonant frequency and the quality factor.

narration.en: Turning a radio's tuning knob changes a capacitor until the circuit resonates with one station's frequency, and the current from that station shoots up. That is series LCR resonance.
narration.kn: ರೇಡಿಯೊದ ಟ್ಯೂನಿಂಗ್ ಗುಂಡಿ ತಿರುಗಿಸಿದಾಗ ಧಾರಕ ಬದಲಾಗಿ ಮಂಡಲವು ಒಂದು ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಅನುನಾದಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಆ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಗರಿಷ್ಠವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದೇ ಶ್ರೇಣಿ LCR ಅನುನಾದ.

body.en: In a series LCR circuit the same current flows through all three. The voltages are out of phase, so they add as phasors: $V^2 = V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2$. The impedance is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$ and $i_m = v_m/Z$. With $i = i_m\sin(\omega t + \phi)$, the phase angle satisfies $\tan\phi = (X_C - X_L)/R$: if X_L > X_C the circuit is inductive and current lags; if X_C > X_L it is capacitive and current leads.
body.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿ LCR ನಲ್ಲಿ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್‌ಗಳು ಫೇಸರ್‌ಗಳಂತೆ ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಬಾಧೆ Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²). X_L > X_C ಆದರೆ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಹಿಂದೆ, X_C > X_L ಆದರೆ ಮುಂದೆ.

narration.en: In series LCR, the voltages add as phasors, giving impedance Z equal to root of R squared plus X L minus X C squared. The phase angle depends on which reactance is bigger.
narration.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿ LCR ನಲ್ಲಿ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್‌ಗಳು ಫೇಸರ್‌ಗಳಂತೆ ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಬಾಧೆ Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²). X_L > X_C ಆದರೆ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಹಿಂದೆ, X_C > X_L ಆದರೆ ಮುಂದೆ.

title.en: On the board: the series LCR circuit

narration.en: A series LCR circuit: the same current flows through R, L and C. Draw the phasors: V_R along the current, V_L a quarter turn ahead of it, V_C a quarter turn behind. The resultant gives the impedance Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) and the phase angle, tan φ = (X_C − X_L)/R. At ω₀ = 1/√(LC) the two reactances cancel, Z = R and the current peaks: that is resonance. The sharpness of the peak is measured by the quality factor Q = ω₀L/R. Example: L = 0.1 H, C = 10 μF and R = 10 Ω give ω₀ = 1000 rad/s, about 159 Hz, and Q = 10.

say.en: A series LCR circuit: the same current flows through R, L and C.
Draw the phasors: V_R along the current, V_L a quarter turn ahead of it, V_C a quarter turn behind.
The resultant gives the impedance Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) and the phase angle, tan φ = (X_C − X_L)/R.
At ω₀ = 1/√(LC) the two reactances cancel, Z = R and the current peaks: that is resonance.
The sharpness of the peak is measured by the quality factor Q = ω₀L/R.
Example: L = 0.1 H, C = 10 μF and R = 10 Ω give ω₀ = 1000 rad/s, about 159 Hz, and Q = 10.

body.en: When X_L = X_C, the reactances cancel: Z = R, its smallest value, and the current is largest and in phase with the voltage. This happens at the resonant frequency $\omega_0 = 1/\sqrt{LC}$. The sharpness of resonance is measured by the quality factor $Q = \omega_0L/R = \frac1R\sqrt{L/C}$; the bandwidth is 2Δω = R/L. A small R gives a high Q and sharp tuning. Resonance needs both L and C.
body.kn: X_L = X_C ಆದಾಗ ಅನುನಾದ: Z = R ಕನಿಷ್ಠ, ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ. ω₀ = 1/√(LC). ಗುಣಮಟ್ಟ ಅಂಶ Q = ω₀L/R; ಕಡಿಮೆ R ಎಂದರೆ ತೀಕ್ಷ್ಣ ಅನುನಾದ.

points.en: Resonance: X_L = X_C, Z = R, current maximum

narration.en: At resonance X L equals X C, the impedance is just R and the current is maximum. The resonant frequency is one over root L C. A small resistance gives a high quality factor and sharp tuning.
narration.kn: X_L = X_C ಆದಾಗ ಅನುನಾದ: Z = R ಕನಿಷ್ಠ, ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ. ω₀ = 1/√(LC). ಗುಣಮಟ್ಟ ಅಂಶ Q = ω₀L/R; ಕಡಿಮೆ R ಎಂದರೆ ತೀಕ್ಷ್ಣ ಅನುನಾದ.

aim.en: To draw the resonance curve of a series LCR circuit and find its resonant frequency and quality factor.

narration.en: Sweep the frequency and record the current. It rises to a sharp peak at the resonant frequency and falls on either side. Increase R and see the peak become lower and broader.

title.en: Resonance curve of a series LCR circuit

caption.en: Current from a 10 V rms source through a series LCR circuit, against frequency. The peak is at f₀ = 1/2π√(LC), where Z = R.

tryThis.en: Set 100 mH, 10 μF, 10 Ω: the peak is near 159 Hz and Q = 10.
Raise R: the peak gets lower and broader, but stays at the same frequency.
Raise C: the peak moves to a lower frequency. This is how a radio is tuned.

narration.en: Current from a 10 V rms source through a series LCR circuit, against frequency. The peak is at f₀ = 1/2π√(LC), where Z = R. Set 100 mH, 10 μF, 10 Ω: the peak is near 159 Hz and Q = 10. Raise R: the peak gets lower and broader, but stays at the same frequency. Raise C: the peak moves to a lower frequency. This is how a radio is tuned.

problem.en: A series circuit has R = 30 Ω, X_L = 80 Ω and X_C = 40 Ω across a 200 V rms supply. Find Z, the current and the phase angle.

steps.en: tan φ = (X_C − X_L)/R = −40/30, so |φ| ≈ 53°, with the current lagging the voltage (inductive).

answer.en: Z = 50 Ω; I = 4 A; current lags by about 53°

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A series circuit has R = 30 Ω, X_L = 80 Ω and X_C = 40 Ω across a 200 V rms supply. Find Z, the current and the phase angle.

problem.en: A series LCR circuit has L = 5.0 H, C = 80 μF and R = 40 Ω, connected to a 230 V variable-frequency source. Find the resonant angular frequency, the current at resonance and Q.

steps.en: At resonance Z = R: I = 230/40 = 5.75 A.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A series LCR circuit has L = 5.0 H, C = 80 μF and R = 40 Ω, connected to a 230 V variable-frequency source. Find the resonant angular frequency, the current at resonance and Q.

body.en: At resonance V_L and V_C are equal and opposite, and each equals Q times the supply voltage. With a high Q they can be many times larger than the supply, even though they cancel each other.

narration.en: Voltages bigger than the supply. At resonance V_L and V_C are equal and opposite, and each equals Q times the supply voltage. With a high Q they can be many times larger than the supply, even though they cancel each other.

mnemonic.en: At resonance: V_L = V_C = Q × V
